subject: URGENT: Peak-window breach — ApexRetail reserved throughput drift & dedicated pool saturation
messages:
From: Platform Alerts <alerts@redwood-monitoring.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:15:22-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 17 saturation and reservation drift (Apex Retail)

Automated alert: Observed sustained GPU utilization > 96% on dedicated pool-17 (us-west-2) for the last 22 minutes.
Concurrent metric: Apex Retail reserved throughput consumption at 102% of committed capacity for their peak window (08:00-09:30 PDT). Token queue depth increased by 3.4x; 95th latency moving from 260ms to 920ms across generation endpoints.

Attached: pool_snapshot_20261003.csv (summary snapshot).

-- Redwood Monitoring

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@apexretail.com (Elena Torres), support@apexretail.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:22:10-07:00
Subject: RE: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 17 saturation and reservation drift (Apex Retail)

Folks —

Thanks for the alerts. Elena / Apex ops: we see the same signal on our side and are treating this as an active customer-impact issue. Short summary: their reserved capacity is being exceeded during the morning peak; the dedicated pool serving their traffic is at sustained saturation and token queueing is causing latency and intermittent 5xx responses.

Immediate asks:
- David: can we confirm whether any background batch jobs or misrouted traffic spiked into pool-17?
- Marcus: can you pull recent kernel/eviction logs and KV cache hit rates for pool-17?
- Irene: I need an estimate for how much burst capacity we can open in the next 20 minutes without violating other commitments.

Elena, I'm proposing an immediate 30-minute operational bridge to agree on a short-term MAP (mutual action plan) and whether we open burst capacity or shift traffic to a compatible lower-memory model until the peak passes. I'm attaching a MAP template and the snapshot from monitoring. Please confirm availability.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee | Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: MAP_ApexRetail_v2.docx, pool_snapshot_20261003.csv

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@apexretail.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:31:05-07:00
Subject: RE: RE: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 17 saturation and reservation drift (Apex Retail)

On it — quick findings:
- No scheduled maintenance or batch reroute in the last 24 hours.
- Telemetry shows a 1.9x increase in concurrent QPS from two API keys owned by Apex (key-A and key-B) starting 07:55 PDT; both map to the reserved project.
- Autoscaler for pool-17 is at configured max (no more nodes in the pool).
- There are a handful of small tenants on the same physical cluster (multi-tenant placement) but their footprint is steady.

I recommend: immediate short-term relief by enabling burst nodes on pool-17 (capacity permitting) and, if necessary, programmatic model-fallback to a quantized variant for non-critical routes. Marcus — logs/eviction dump upload in 5 mins.

-David
David Kim | Sr. Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@apexretail.com
Date: 2026-10-03T08:36:54-07:00
Subject: RE: RE: RE: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 17 saturation and reservation drift (Apex Retail)

Uploaded: capacity_headroom_plot.png and detailed_eviction_log.txt (reference in drive link). Quick notes from kernel & runtime traces:
- KV cache hit-rate decreased from 86% to 55% during the surge; large-context requests (seq_len > 1024) spiked and forced repeated KV refills.
- A small number (~12) of requests are using a legacy large-decoder model (gpt-large-legacy) that is 2-3x more memory hungry — suspecting a misrouted key or recent client rollout.
- We can open 2 burst nodes within 10 minutes if ops approves; beyond that we need cross-pool placement which takes ~25-30 minutes.

Immediate mitigation plan (short):
1) Authorize 2 burst nodes on pool-17 (10 min spin-up)
2) Apply a temporary QoS cap on apex non-critical routes (drop to quantized model)
3) If demand persists, initiate traffic shift to pool-21 and failover routing.

If execs want a single action: authorize burst nodes now. Otherwise we start a multi-step handoff.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin | Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <ops@apexretail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T08:42:11-07:00
Subject: Re: RE: RE: RE: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 17 saturation and reservation drift (Apex Retail)

Thanks for the quick triage. We just deployed a client-side experiment this morning that increases request concurrency for low-latency personalization calls — that likely explains the QPS bump. We can temporarily revert the rollout if that helps.

We approve any short-term burst capacity you can open immediately. If you open burst nodes, can you commit to preserving our reserved throughput once the peak subsides (we need guarantee on no cross-tenant eviction for our reserved commitments)?

Also: please invite our SRE (sre@apexretail.com) to any ops bridge you spin up.

— Elena

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@apexretail.com
Date: 2026-10-03T09:17:05-07:00
Subject: Exec note — immediate authorization & customer protections

Looping in as requested. Soojin — thanks for the heads-up. Approving the following immediate actions:
- Authorize 2 burst nodes to pool-17 now (David / Marcus: proceed).
- Apply temporary QoS cap and programmatic fallback for non-critical endpoints (Marcus to coordinate).
- We will not reallocate any core reserved slots for Apex while they remain within contractual windows; any overage will be billed per contract but prioritize customer reliability first.

Soojin: pull together a short customer-facing summary for Elena (one paragraph) confirming what we did and their options/next steps; include the MAP doc and a proposed timeline for a post-incident root-cause (RCA). We need to close the loop on whether a client rollout caused the spike and whether the placement policy needs tightening.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | VP, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
